Athenian procedure by which citizens could vote to exile for 10 years a man judged dangerous for democracy. Names were inscribed on pottery shards (ostrakon). Its objective was preventive, not punitive.

Unlike almost all substances, water is denser at 4°C than at 0°C. As it cools from 4°C to 0°C, it expands. This density anomaly of water is essential for aquatic life: ice floats and insulates the liquid water beneath it.

Water evaporates from the oceans, leaving salts behind. It falls back as rain, dissolves minerals from rocks, and carries them to the oceans via rivers. This accumulation process has been ongoing for 4 billion years.

The 23.5° tilt of Earth's axis relative to its orbital plane - and not the distance from the Sun - causes the seasons. The same tilt always points toward the North Star, alternately creating solstices and equinoxes.

The points in the orbit closest to (perihelion, in January) and farthest from (aphelion, in July) the Sun. The difference in distance is 5%, too small to explain the seasons. Paradoxically, the northern winter coincides with the perihelion.

Contagious yawning is linked to mirror neurons and contagiousness which mimic observed behaviors. Humans are more sensitive to the yawns of people they know, and autistic children are less sensitive to them - evidence of a link with empathy.

Seahorse-shaped brain structure in the temporal lobe, essential for forming new conscious memories. Its surgical removal (case H.M.) leads to a total inability to form new memories, without erasing old ones.

A molecule with one hydrophilic end (water-loving) and one hydrophobic end (fat-loving). This double nature allows it to insert itself into the lipid membranes of viruses and physically disintegrate them.

Some viruses (coronavirus, flu, HIV) are surrounded by a fatty membrane. This is their weak point: soap dissolves it, destroying the virus. Non-enveloped viruses (norovirus, poliovirus) are more resistant to soap.

A spontaneous phenomenon by which an unstable atomic nucleus transforms by emitting particles (alpha, beta) or radiation (gamma). Marie Curie understood that radioactivity was a property of the atom itself, not a chemical reaction.

Röntgen and his first users were unaware of the dangers of X-rays. Doctors developed cancers after years of exposure. Marie Curie herself died of aplastic anemia caused by her years of contact with radioactive materials.

An evolutionary phenomenon by which bacteria develop mechanisms to resist antibiotics. Predicted by Fleming as early as 1945, it now kills 1.27 million people per year - one of the main health threats of the 21st century.
The triumph of the capture of Granada released resources and created a momentum of national ambition that explains Isabella of Castile's support for Columbus.
An agreement arbitrated by the Pope dividing the world into two spheres of influence between Spain (west) and Portugal (east).

Even before anesthesia, post-operative infections killed patients. Semmelweis (1847) then Lister (1867) imposed hygiene: hand washing, sterilized instruments. These two revolutions - anesthesia and antisepsis - transformed surgery.
Sovereign of the United Kingdom whose use of chloroform during her childbirths in 1853 and 1857 helped to remove religious taboos regarding anesthesia.
Royal Navy ship that served as a base for Charles Darwin for his scientific tour of the World between 1831 and 1836.

Discovered in 1998, the expansion of the universe is accelerating instead of slowing down. This acceleration is attributed to "Dark energy" (68% of the total content of the universe), which remains completely misunderstood by current physics.
Ductile part of the Earth's upper mantle located beneath the rigid lithosphere, allowing the movement of tectonic plates.
Field of civil engineering studying the design and construction of buildings capable of resisting seismic shocks without collapsing.

Nom du cours: Is there life elsewhere in the Universe?
Explication: Region around a star where the temperature allows water to exist in a liquid state on a planet's surface. Neither too close nor too far - "like Goldilocks". Our solar system has three potential planets: Venus, Earth, Mars.

Nom du cours: Is there life elsewhere in the Universe?
Explication: Probabilistic formula by Frank Drake (1961) to estimate the number of communicating civilizations in our galaxy. It multiplies factors (stars, habitable planets, duration of civilizations...) - all values being very uncertain, making the equation more philosophical than scientific.
"Boundary" of a black hole beyond which nothing can return, not even light. It is not a physical surface but a mathematical limit: the speed required to escape exceeds that of light.

For a lightning bolt to form, the electric field must be intense enough to strip electrons from air molecules, making it conductive. This channel forms in a few microseconds, heated to 30,000°C - five times the sun's surface.
White blood cells that produce antibodies - proteins capable of recognizing and neutralizing a specific pathogen. After vaccination, some become "memory cells" that sometimes persist for a lifetime.

When a sufficient proportion of the population is immunized, the pathogen can no longer spread, indirectly protecting non-immunized people. The threshold varies from 80% to 95% depending on the disease.

The ability of a surface to reflect solar radiation. Ice and snow have a high albedo (reflect a lot), oceans have a low albedo (absorb more). Melting ice reduces the global albedo, accelerating warming.

Internal clock set to 24 hours, regulated by the suprachiasmatic nucleus of the brain. Melatonin, produced at night, signals the need to sleep. Artificial nocturnal light disrupts this rhythm and degrades sleep quality.

A tiny jellyfish capable of returning to its juvenile polyp stage after the adult stage - and starting over indefinitely. This process of cellular transdifferentiation is unique and inspires research on cellular reprogramming.

A mysterious force responsible for the acceleration of the universe's expansion, representing 68% of its total content. Distinct from dark matter (27%), it acts as a repulsive energy of the vacuum, still completely misunderstood.
Physics Theory that describes elementary particles (quarks, electrons, etc.) and three of the four fundamental forces, but fails to explain dark matter.

Nom du cours: How does electricity work in our bodies?
Explication: Sea-horse-shaped brain structure in the temporal lobe, essential for the formation of new conscious memories. Its surgical removal (case H.M.) leads to a total inability to form new memories, without erasing old ones.

Nom du cours: How does electricity work in our bodies?
Explication: Cognitive system that temporarily maintains a small amount of information (7±2 items) available for current processing. Managed by the prefrontal cortex, it is limited in capacity and duration (a few seconds without repetition).

Nom du cours: How does electricity work in our bodies?
Explication: Contracts by which buyers and sellers commit to a future transaction at a price fixed today. Speculators with no intention of physical delivery represent the vast majority of transactions, amplifying price fluctuations.

Nom du cours: How does electricity work in our bodies?
Explication: Massive boom in American production in the 21st century thanks to hydraulic fracturing, modifying the world's geopolitical energy balance.

Nom du cours: Why do certain sounds give us chills?
Explication: Personality trait associated with curiosity and the appreciation of beauty. People who are highly "open" have an auditory cortex more connected to emotional zones and are significantly more likely to feel musical chills.

Nom du cours: Why do seasons exist on other planets?
Explication: Uranus's axis is almost lying flat on its orbital plane. Each pole receives about 42 years of continuous sunlight and then 42 years of total darkness - extreme seasons of very long duration, with no equivalent in our solar system.

Nom du cours: Why do seasons exist on other planets?
Explication: Mars's orbit is significantly more elliptical than Earth's: the Sun-Mars distance varies from 207 to 249 million km. The Martian southern hemisphere has short, hot summers and long, cold winters - much more marked than here.

The Homeric epics were composed orally before being written down. Repeated formulas ("Rosy-fingered Dawn", "Odysseus of many wiles") facilitated memorization and improvised composition - a Technique studied by Milman Parry in the 20th century.

Literary genre of the epic: a long sequence where a hero performs superhuman feats. Each great warrior of the Iliad has his aristeia. These passages allowed the hero's character to be developed and his lineage to be linked to the gods.

Terme: Fate and free will in Greek tragedy
Explication: Tragedy explores the tension between inevitable fate (predicted by oracles) and human choices. Oedipus fulfills his tragic destiny precisely while attempting to flee it - a paradox at the heart of the human condition according to the Greeks.

Tension at the heart of Antigone: divine and moral Law (burying the dead) against the human Law of Creon. This conflict runs through all political philosophy, from Plato to Rousseau and modern theorists of natural rights.

The hubris (excess, excessive pride) is the quintessential Greek tragic sin. Creon commits hubris by believing that his Law takes precedence over that of the gods - he will lose everything he loved as punishment for this presumption.

Plato distinguishes between physical love and spiritual love aspiring to absolute Beauty. Diotima's speech describes a "ladder of love": starting from a beautiful body, then loving the beauty of souls, then ideal Beauty-itself.
Three divine sisters born old, possessing only one eye and one tooth between them, guardians of the path to the Gorgon.
Sea nymphs, daughters of Nereus, offended by the vanity of Queen Cassiopeia.
Divinities in charge of human destiny, represented as spinners (the Roman equivalent of the Moirai).
A public building in Athens where magistrates sat and where deserving citizens and victorious athletes were fed at the city's expense.

Terme: Revenge and honor in the Greek world
Explication: Honor (timē) was a fundamental value in Greece. A betrayal demanded reparation. Medea cannot accept the dishonor of being repudiated: her revenge follows a logic of reciprocity which, pushed to the extreme, becomes monstrous.

Terme: Penal colony and the 19th-century penal system
Explication: The penal colonies of Toulon, Brest, and Rochefort were hells of forced labor. Jean Valjean spent 19 years there for a stolen loaf of bread, illustrating the brutality of a system that did not distinguish between crime and poverty.
The incorruptible police officer who pursues Jean Valjean. He personifies the strict and blind Law, incapable of conceiving of forgiveness or the moral evolution of a criminal.

The philosophy according to which God created the best of all possible worlds and that apparent evil serves a higher good. Voltaire wrote Candide in response, notably to the Lisbon earthquake (1755) which killed 60,000 people in a few minutes.

A feeling born from the clash between the human desire for meaning and the silence of the universe. Camus does not see the absurd as a cosmic truth but as a lived experience - the response is not suicide but lucid and conscious rebellion.

The Stranger takes place in 1940s French Algeria. The Arab that Meursault kills remains nameless in the novel - a major postcolonial critique: the novel is said to reproduce the invisibility of Arabs in French colonial literature.

A project of 90 interconnected novels and short stories describing the totality of French society. Figures return from one novel to another - an innovation that was unprecedented at the time. Rastignac appears in about twenty works within the cycle.

Baudelaire is the father of symbolism: he sought not to describe reality but to suggest secret correspondences between sensations, emotions, and ideas. Verlaine, Rimbaud, and Mallarmé, and later the entire Poetics of the 20th century, claim his influence.

Old Major = Marx/Lenin, Napoleon = Stalin, Snowball = Trotsky, Squealer = propaganda. The progressively modified commandments illustrate the betrayal of revolutionary ideals by the bureaucracy in power.

Revenge is a central theme of Elizabethan theater. A man of honor had to avenge an offense to his family - but this duty conflicted with the Law and Christian morality. This paradox fuels Hamlet's fundamental hesitation.

A literary tradition glorifying the secret and suffering love of a knight for a lady (often married). Romeo begins the play in this stereotypical role (in love with Rosaline) before his love for Juliet becomes real and tragic.
Here, an attitude that consists of mocking ideal values and feelings through a critical spirit or disillusionment, as Mercutio does.

Industrial organization methods that rationalized production through extreme division of labor and the assembly line. Huxley applies them to human reproduction and conditioning - Ford is the deity of the novel.

The 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora ejected ash that darkened the global atmosphere, causing a freezing summer in Europe in 1816. It was in this apocalyptic context that Mary Shelley (18 years old) wrote Frankenstein during a stay on the shores of Lake Geneva.

Don Quixote is one of the first novels to comment on itself: in the second part (1615), the figures have read the first part (1605) and discuss it. This play with the reality of the novel anticipates literary postmodernism by several centuries.

Terme: Battle of Lepanto (1571) and Cervantes' captivity
Explication: Cervantes fought at Lepanto and was wounded (losing the use of his left hand). Captured by pirates in 1575, he was an enslaved person in Algiers for five years. These experiences forged the writer and nourished the humor and depth of the novel.
A superior force that guides human events toward a determined end, often identified here with divine will.
Three divine sisters born old, sharing only one eye and one tooth between them, guardians of the path to the Gorgons.
Sea nymphs, daughters of Nereus, offended by the vanity of Queen Cassiopeia.
Divinities in charge of human destiny, represented as spinners (the Roman equivalent of the Moirai).

Bradbury anticipated self-censorship through entertainment: people so saturated with fast-paced media that they no longer have the desire to read. The "parlors" (wall-screens) in the novel anticipate television and then smartphones.
A superior force that guides human events toward a specific end, often identified here with divine will.
A major work of world Literature (1915) recounting the sudden transformation of Gregor Samsa into an insect.
Three divine sisters born old, possessing only one eye and one tooth for the three of them, guardians of the path to the Gorgons.
Sea nymphs, daughters of Nereus, offended by the vanity of Queen Cassiopeia.

Deities in charge of human destiny, represented as spinners (Roman equivalent of the Moirai).

Novel by Paulo Coelho published in 1988, telling the initiatory quest of a shepherd named Santiago.

Intellectual movement centering reflection on the human being, inspired by rediscovered Greek and Roman texts. Humanists (Petrarch, Erasmus) valued liberal education, human dignity, and the development of individual faculties.
The invention of metal paint tubes (1841) allowed painters to work outdoors. This innovation was a material condition for the Impressionist revolution.

Terme: African and Oceanic art as influence
Explication: Picasso's discovery of African masks around 1906-1907 was a revelation: an art that did not seek to imitate reality but to provide a symbolic and structural representation of it. Decisive for the Demoiselles d'Avignon.

Surrealist Technique: writing or painting without conscious control, letting the flow of the unconscious express itself directly. Breton used it as a Poetics tool. Dalí developed his own pictorial variant with the paranoiac-critical method.

Terme: German Expressionism (Die Brücke, Der Blaue Reiter)
Explication: German artistic currents (1905-1920) pushing expressionism to the extreme: radical distortion of forms, gaudy colors, distressing themes. Kirchner, Kandinsky, Nolde reacted to modernization and heralded the trauma of 1914.

Terme: Eruption of Krakatoa (1883) and the red sky
Explication: The catastrophic eruption of Krakatoa threw up ash that colored sunsets blood-red around the World for months. Munch noted in his diary having seen a red sky "of blood and fire" — likely this phenomenon.

School of art and design founded in Weimar in 1919 which attempted to reconcile fine arts and applied arts. Kandinsky and Klee taught there. Its minimalist and functional aesthetic is omnipresent in contemporary design.

Benjamin (1935) analyzed how technical reproduction destroys the "aura" of the unique Work. Warhol radicalized this idea: by mechanically reproducing popular images, he questioned the very notion of original and author.

House (Chicago, 1984) used drum machines and deep bass lines. Techno (Detroit, 1986-1988) was colder and more mechanical. Both emerged from marginalized Black and Latino communities and became world phenomena.

Two Italian genres: opera seria (noble subjects, tragic) and opera buffa (comic subjects, ordinary characters). Verdi excelled in opera seria but renewed the genres by integrating realistic psychological drama and social tension.

The absolute music (Beethoven) expresses pure emotions without external reference. Program music (Berlioz, Liszt) tells a story. This distinction structures the great aesthetic debate of the romantic 19th century.

The last movement of the 9th Symphony, based on Schiller's poem, became the official anthem of the European Union in 1985. The universalism of its message (brotherhood of humanity) makes it the symbol of the European ideal of unity.

Counterpoint is the art of combining several independent melodies according to harmonic rules. The fugue is its most elaborate form: a theme is stated by different voices in turn, then developed in increasingly complex combinations.

Unlike classical music, jazz makes improvisation its heart: the musician invents their melodic line in real time, over an agreed harmonic grid, in response to the others. It is both total freedom and a demanding discipline.

Nom du cours: The blues: roots of all modern music
Explication: Three divine sisters born old, possessing only one eye and one tooth between the three, guardians of the path to the Gorgons.

Terme: Impact of photography on figurative painting
Explication: Photography liberated painting from its documentary function. Painters no longer had to immortalize faces or battles - photography did it better and cheaper. This liberation was one of the conditions for Impressionism and then abstraction.

Terme: Filming on location and lightweight camera
Explication: The French New Wave technically reinvented cinema: lightweight portable cameras, fast film allowing filming without artificial lighting. These budgetary constraints became a revolutionary aesthetic - cinema "taking to the streets".

HAL 9000 is one of the first representations of a conscious AI in conflict with its creators. Its anthropomorphism (calm voice, implacable logic, self-preservation) prefigures current debates about AI safety.

Structural innovations of Gothic architecture. The rib vault distributes the weight onto ribs rather than the entire walls. The flying buttress transfers the thrust outwards, allowing walls to be opened into windows without the building collapsing.
Abbot of Saint-Denis and advisor to the kings of France, considered the father of Gothic art through his Reconstruction of the Basilica of Saint-Denis.
Central Concept for Van Gogh where the Work does not seek to reproduce physical reality but the emotions and visions of the painter.

Art critic for "Le Charivari", Louis Leroy wrote a sarcastic article in 1874: "Impression, I was certain of it!". He wanted to mock them - the term "impressionists" was adopted by the artists themselves with pride, turning the insult around.

Le Havre was the leading French commercial port, transformed by industrialization. Monet shows precisely this industrial modernity (steam, cranes, small boats) in the morning mist - a fleeting vision of modernity on the move.

Nighthawks was painted in 1942, a few weeks after Pearl Harbor. The isolation of the Figure in the American night translates a deep unease: the individualism of American society, the absence of community, the void behind material abundance.

Bergson distinguished between physical time (measurable) and lived time (subjective, elastic). The melting watches of Dalí visually illustrate this "Bergsonian time": in dreams, time expands, contracts, and loses all rigidity.

Nom du cours: Freedom of the press and photojournalism
Explication: Fundamental tension: how far should a photographer get involved? Kevin Carter photographed a vulture waiting for the death of a Sudanese child (1993) and was accused of not helping. He received the Pulitzer and then committed suicide three months later.

Nom du cours: Freedom of the press and photojournalism
Explication: In many democracies, billionaires (Murdoch, Bolloré) have bought up media outlets, raising questions about their independence. In France in 2024, the vast majority of the press is owned by a dozen billionaires.

Nom du cours: Freedom of the press and photojournalism
Explication: Three divine sisters born old, possessing only one eye and one tooth for the three of them, guardians of the path to the Gorgon.

Nom du cours: Freedom of the press and photojournalism
Explication: Divinities in charge of human destiny, represented as spinners (Roman equivalent of the Moirai).

Nom du cours: The birth of the Greek gods (Cronus, Zeus, Olympus)
Explication: The Greek gods are entirely human in their emotions (jealousy, love, anger) but immortal and supernatural. Xenophanes already criticized this vision: "if horses had gods, they would represent them as horses".

Brother of Prometheus whose name means "the one who thinks after". He thoughtlessly accepted Pandora's gift sent by Zeus. His recklessness introduced evils into the World. The Prometheus-Epimetheus pair illustrates the opposition between foresight and impulsivity.

In Hesiod's version, Hope remains in the jar when Pandora closes it. A fundamental ambiguity: is it the last benevolent gift from the gods, or an additional evil (false hope, illusion) that tortures men by making them believe things will improve?

The descent into the Underworld. A recurring mythological motif: the hero descends into the Underworld alive (Heracles, Odysseus, Aeneas, Orpheus). This journey symbolizes initiation through death and confrontation with the unconscious.

Greek mystic religion. A religious movement inspired by the myth of Orpheus, advocating for the purification of the soul and metempsychosis (transmigration of souls). It influenced Pythagoras and Plato in their conception of the immortality of the soul.

Term coined by Freud (1914): excessive love for oneself, inability to love the Other. In the myth, Narcissus cannot love Echo because he only loves his own image. Freud distinguished primary narcissism (healthy) from pathological narcissism.

The repercussion of a sound against a surface and its return to its source. The word "echo" comes directly from the nymph of the myth, condemned to only repeat the last words heard. This myth explained the natural acoustic phenomenon to the Greeks.

Icarus embodies classic hubris: failing to respect human limits and seeking to rise to the gods' level. This transgression is always punished in Greek Mythology - the Greeks saw excess as the tragic fault par excellence.

In The Myth of Sisyphus (1942), Camus chooses this myth because Sisyphus knows his fate and continues anyway. Camus concludes that "one must imagine Sisyphus happy" - only the refusal of resignation makes the absurd bearable.

Sisyphus was punished for having cheated death twice and revealed secrets of the gods. In Greek Mythology, mortals who defied divine order or claimed immortality received eternal and exemplary punishments.
Named so in 1802 by Ekeberg because it is insoluble in acids - like Tantalus who cannot swallow anything. It is used in smartphone capacitors and in biocompatible medical prostheses.

When Perseus beheads Medusa, the winged horse Pegasus is born from her blood. He would be captured by Bellerophon with the help of Athena and would allow him to defeat the Chimera. Pegasus has become the universal symbol of Poetics inspiration.

Greek heroism (Hercules, Achilles) values strength, warrior glory, and prowess - even if Hercules acts out of penitence. Christian heroism values humility, sacrifice, and accepted suffering. This tension structures Western culture.

Practical intelligence, cunning, the ability to turn an unfavorable situation around. Odysseus embodies metis par excellence - his Homeric epithet is "of many wiles". It stands in opposition to bié (brute force) embodied by Ajax.

One-eyed beings, sons of Ouranos and Gaia: divine blacksmiths who forged the thunderbolts of Zeus. In Homer, Polyphemus and his kind are wild shepherds ignorant of the gods and the laws - an embodiment of barbarism.
Decision-making strategy consisting of voluntarily restricting one's future options to counter an anticipated temptation.

Region to the east of the Black Sea, described in Greek myths as the end of the eastern World. Shepherds there used sheep fleeces to filter gold from the gold-bearing rivers of the Caucasus - the "golden fleece" might have been real.

Supreme value of heroic culture: the immortal glory acquired through exploits in war and transmitted by poets. Achilles deliberately chooses a short but glorious life rather than a long life without glory - a fundamental choice of Greek heroic ethics.

Oedipus's incest (unintentional) represents the ultimate transgression of social order: the confusion of generations. For the Greeks, it provoked a defilement (miasma) affecting the entire community, visible in the pestilence striking Thebes.

Nom du cours: Antigone: family duty vs. state law
Explication: Play performed in Paris during the Nazi Occupation. Anouilh deliberately left its political reading ambiguous: Creon could represent the Germans or Vichy, Antigone the Resistance. Both sides found what they were looking for in the Work - genius or opportunism?

Nom du cours: The Trojan War and the wooden horse
Explication: Schliemann located Troy in 1870 at Hisarlik, Turkey. Excavations brought to light nine successive cities. Troy VIIa (around 1184 BC) shows traces of fire compatible with Homer's account - the Trojan War may have taken place.

Nom du cours: The Trojan War and the wooden horse
Explication: Circular plan building, used here to designate the underground chamber where Danaë was imprisoned.

13th-century Icelandic treatise on Poetics and Mythology. Although written in a Christian context, it constitutes the most structured source on Norse beliefs, intended to preserve the Art of ancient poetry.
Medieval manuscript containing a collection of mythological and heroic poems in Old Norse, considered a complementary and often older source than the Prose Edda.

Nom du cours: Ragnarök: the end of the Norse world
Explication: Norse cosmic ash tree connecting the nine worlds. Its roots delve into the realms of the gods, the Giants, and the dead. The Norns (weavers of fate) live at its base. The cosmic tree is a near-universal mythological archetype.

Nom du cours: Ragnarök: the end of the Norse world
Explication: The vision of Ragnarök shares traits with other eschatologies: the Christian Last Judgment, the Hindu Kali Yuga. These apocalyptic visions reflect a universal concern for the end of times and, often, the Renaissance that follows.

Fundamental principle of Egyptian thought: cosmic order, truth, and justice. The pharaoh was responsible for maintaining Ma'at against chaos. Osiris presides over the judgment of the dead, weighing their hearts against the feather of Ma'at.

Nom du cours: Romulus and Remus: the founding of Rome
Explication: Traditional Date of the founding of Rome (753 BC), calculated by Varro in the 1st century BC. The Romans counted years "since the founding of the city" (AUC). This Legendary Date corresponded to the monarchy of the seven kings of Rome.

Samsara: cycle of reincarnations of the soul. Karma: Law of moral causality - every action has consequences for future lives. Vishnu descends to Earth in avatars specifically to restore disrupted cosmic Karma.

Norse warriors sought to die with weapons in hand to be chosen by the Valkyries. Dying of illness ("straw death") did not open the gates of Valhalla—this vision of a warrior paradise structured Viking culture.

Terme: Order and chaos in Greek mythology
Explication: The Titanomachy represents the victory of Olympian order (Zeus, reason, Law) over the primordial chaos of the Titans. This narrative structure—a cosmic struggle between order and chaos—is found in all the great World mythologies.

After the Titanomachy, the Olympians had to face the Giants (born from the blood of Uranus), who were nearly invincible. This second war of the gods foreshadows the permanent tensions between Olympian order and the primordial forces of chaos.

Nom du cours: Dionysus: the god of wine and excess
Explication: Philosophical opposition between order/reason (Apollo) and chaos/drunkenness (Dionysus) as drivers of artistic creation.

Nom du cours: Aeneas and the founding of Rome (Virgil)
Explication: Legendary conflict pitting the Greek states against the Trojans, serving as the chronological starting point for the Aeneid.

Terme: Cosmology of the Five Suns and cosmic debt
Explication: The gods had sacrificed their blood to create the fifth sun. Humans were in perpetual debt and had to repay it with blood. This logic of cosmic exchange made sacrifices morally necessary in the Aztec vision of the World.

The 18 chapters of dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna constitute a major philosophical text, independent of the rest of the epic. Krishna teaches selfless action (Karma yoga), devotion (bhakti), and knowledge (jnana) as paths to liberation.

Terme: Orality and transmission of Indian epics (Concept)
Explication: Like Homer, The Mahabharata was originally an oral epic memorized and recited by griots. Its transcription stretched over several centuries. These texts are still recited and sung throughout India, as alive as ever.

Nom du cours: Lancelot, Guinevere and the Round Table
Explication: Social code glorifying the secret and inaccessible love of a knight for a lady (often married). Lancelot and Guinevere are the perfect example. This adulterous passion, destructive yet sublime, is at the heart of medieval Literature.

Nom du cours: Lancelot, Guinevere and the Round Table
Terme: Quest for the Holy Grail and medieval Christianity
Explication: The Grail was christianized: chalice of the Last Supper or cup that collected the blood of Christ. The quest becomes a spiritual quest for purity. Only Galahad - pure and sinless - can achieve it. Lancelot, tainted by his love for Guinevere, fails.

Nom du cours: Lancelot, Guinevere and the Round Table
Explication: Founding episode where Arthur proves his royal blood by pulling the sword Excalibur (or an anonymous sword according to sources) from a rock or an anvil, proving his divine Legitimacy.

Terme: Archmage in literature, figure of the
Explication: Merlin is the prototype of the archmage: Gandalf (Tolkien), Dumbledore (Rowling) are direct descendants. The wise old man with mysterious powers who guides the hero is a quasi-universal narrative archetype.

Fascination and idealization of the East by Europeans, often stereotyped. One Thousand and One Nights, notably in Antoine Galland's translation (1704), fueled this orientalism: harems, Caliphs, genies became the standard image of the Arab World in Europe.

Marco Polo (1254-1324) made the opposite journey of Sinbad: from Venice to the China of Kublai Khan. His stories seemed as fabulous as those of Sinbad. The Book of Marvels directly influenced Columbus in his plans to travel to Asia.

Nom du cours: The Titans vs the Gods: the complete Titanomachy
Terme: Order and chaos in Greek mythology
Explication: The Titanomachy represents the victory of Olympian order (Zeus, reason, Law) over the primordial chaos of the Titans. This narrative structure - cosmic combat between order and chaos - is found in all major world mythologies.

Starting in 2018, the United States (Trump) imposed massive customs duties on Chinese products, which China responded to in kind. This trade war reflects a technological and geopolitical rivalry deeper than mere exchanges.

American Politics which recognizes "one China" without recognizing Beijing's sovereignty over Taiwan, and sells weapons without explicitly promising a military defense. This deliberate strategic ambiguity is intended to deter invasion while avoiding provoking Beijing.

Krauthammer described (1990) the post-Cold War era as a "unipolar moment" with the United States as the sole superpower. He predicted it would last 30 to 40 years - an accurate prediction, as the "unipolar moment" ended around 2008-2010.
A vast infrastructure and investment project launched by China in 2013 to link Asia, Europe, and Africa, strengthening its global geopolitical weight.

Nom du cours: Oil as a source of conflict
Explication: Economic paradox: countries rich in natural resources (oil, diamonds) often experience slower growth and more frequent conflicts. The oil "rent" creates predatory states and discourages economic diversification.

Nom du cours: The Suez Canal: why it is strategic
Explication: A 400m container ship that ran aground across the canal for 6 days, blocking 400 ships. It cost the World economy 400 million dollars per hour, perfectly illustrating the strategic importance of the canal in global chains.

Nom du cours: NATO: what is its purpose today?
Terme: Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty
Explication: Collective defense clause: an attack against one member is an attack against all. Invoked only once in the History of NATO - on September 12, 2001, after September 11. Its exact scope remains deliberately ambiguous.

Nom du cours: NATO: what is its purpose today?
Explication: Since 1991, NATO has welcomed 14 new members, including former Soviet republics. Russia considers this enlargement an existential threat - an argument used to justify the invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

The Soviet KGB was dissolved in 1991 and replaced by the FSB (domestic) and the SVR (foreign). Putin, a former KGB officer in Dresden, has extensively promoted former members of the KGB (the "siloviki") to key positions in Russian power.

An industrial region in eastern Ukraine where pro-Russian separatists proclaimed "republics" with Russian military support in 2014. This "low intensity" conflict (14,000 deaths) preceded the full-scale invasion on February 24, 2022.

A seahorse-shaped brain structure in the temporal lobe, essential for forming new conscious memories. Its surgical removal (case H.M.) leads to a total inability to form new memories without erasing old ones.

A cognitive system that temporarily maintains a small amount of information (7±2 items) available for ongoing processing. Managed by the prefrontal cortex, it is limited in capacity and duration (a few seconds without rehearsal).

An all-or-nothing electrical signal triggered when the depolarization of a neuron exceeds a threshold. It propagates along the axon at 1 to 100 m/s depending on myelination. It is the "click" of information that the neuron sends.

Chemical molecules released in the synapse that transmit signals between neurons. The main ones: glutamate (excitatory), GABA (inhibitory), dopamine, serotonin. Psychoactive drugs act on these systems.

An agreement signed by 136 countries to impose a 15% minimum rate on multinational profits, regardless of their country of filing. The first major international tax agreement in History, it aims to end the tax "race to the bottom."

For Keynes (1936), the state must borrow to spend during recessions. Public debt is an economic management tool, not a moral issue. This Theory justifies recovery plans such as the New Deal or post-COVID stimulus.

A platform becomes more valuable as the number of users increases. Facebook, Uber, Amazon: the more users there are, the better the service, which attracts even more users - creating virtually insurmountable natural monopolies.

An economy of "piecework" where individuals offer their services via platforms without permanent contracts. It weakens traditional social protections (retirement, unemployment) while offering flexibility for workers.

Terme: Arctic sea ice and albedo effect
Explication: Unlike sea ice (the melting of which does not raise water levels), the melting of ice in Greenland and Antarctica raises the oceans directly. Furthermore, dark water replacing white ice absorbs more heat, accelerating warming.

Storms combined with rising sea levels create temporary "surges" well above the average level. A 50 cm rise in sea levels can multiply the frequency of floods previously described as "hundred-year floods" by 10 - Rare events become common.
Type of artificial intelligence capable of creating new content (text, images, code, sound) from learned examples, rather than simply analyzing existing data.

Nom du cours: Mental health as a societal issue
Explication: Chronic exhaustion syndrome caused by overwork, recognized by the WHO since 2019 as an occupational phenomenon. It is characterized by emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and a reduced sense of accomplishment.

Explication: Psychologist Jonathan Haidt argues that the massive adoption of smartphones by adolescents starting in 2012 is the primary cause of the epidemic of depression and anxiety among young people. The scientific debate remains intense.

Nom du cours: The EU: how does it really work?
Terme: Unanimity in the Council of the EU
Explication: In many areas (taxation, foreign politics), decisions require the unanimity of the 27 member states. A single state can block – which makes the EU difficult to govern during crises and explains its often-criticized slow decision-making.

Fundamental tension: how far should a photographer get involved? Kevin Carter photographed a vulture waiting for the death of a Sudanese child (1993) and was accused of not helping. He received the Pulitzer then committed suicide three months later.

In many democracies, billionaires (Murdoch, Bolloré) have bought up media outlets, raising questions about their independence. In France in 2024, the vast majority of the press is owned by a dozen billionaires.
Three divine sisters born old, sharing only one eye and one tooth between the three, guardians of the path to the Gorgons.

Concept from theorist Antonio Gramsci: a dominant class maintains its power by making its values accepted as natural and universal. Joseph Nye adapted this idea to international relations with the concept of soft power.

European regulatory standards (GDPR, food standards, environmental standards) are adopted globally by multinationals wishing to access the market of 450 million consumers. The EU thus exercises considerable regulatory soft power.

Digital platforms tend toward natural monopolies: each new user increases the value for all others. Competing with Facebook or Amazon becomes almost impossible because their network advantage is insurmountable for a new competitor.

Treaty signed by 196 countries to limit warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels. Each country sets its own targets (NDCs) - current ambitions lead to approximately 2.5°C of warming according to current projections.

Hydrogen produced through water electrolysis powered by renewable energies. It allows for energy storage and the decarbonization of sectors that are difficult to electrify (steel, cement, aviation). Currently expensive, it is seen as key for carbon neutrality 2050.
